_doc: Mined claims for analysis/argument/product agents. Internal only — paraphrase on site; no external author names in rendered contracts.

snippets.claim: GB transmission entry capacity queue exceeds 125 GW with multi-year wait times; demand-side reform treats flexible/non-firm connection as primary queue-clearing lever.
Ofgem Access SCR (Apr 2023) standardised infirm/interruptible/curtailable connection terms across DNOs — firmness becomes a contractual and register-visible attribute.
Industry catalogues dozens of >$1bn non-damage business interruption losses (nat cat, infrastructure failure) where indemnity BI triggers failed or paid late.
Parametric NDBI products typically require 3–5 years from launch to meaningful London Market adoption — generational product cycle, not quarterly feature.
Global data-centre insurance premium projected from ~$10.6bn (2024) toward ~$24bn by 2030 as AI load concentrates insurable values.

Standard London Market BI/DSU wordings require material damage to insured property (or insured peril extension) before interruption indemnity attaches — lawful curtailment without damage sits outside the trigger.
SLA parametric for data centres mirrors tenant SLA metrics (uptime/availability) with telemetry verification — pays on index breach independent of physical damage.
Clarke (2011): rational demand for imperfect index insurance when basis risk r is below a threshold — supports parametric availability cover even when register index ≠ account P&L.
Cyber accumulation PML estimates span orders of magnitude across reinsurers, governments, and model vendors — the disagreement itself proves architectural opacity, not missing data.
snippets.quote_paraphrase: Map to NFRI: curtailment severity at constraint boundary has no licensed stochastic event set — expert ranges would diverge similarly.

snippets.claim: Nat-cat market rebuilt after Andrew (1992) and 1906 SF — hazard modules, event sets, and capital channels emerged because physical damage was observable and correlatable.
Market taxonomy by generation (1.0 indemnity → 2.0 parametric/MGA → 3.0 outside-in accumulation control) clarifies why NFRI is a 3.0 measurement problem for grid availability.
NESO balancing and constraint management costs trend upward as renewable and demand growth concentrate flows — observable proxy for curtailment pressure on non-firm connections.
Broker research frames utility failure and grid curtailment as emerging NDBI/DSU sub-perils for hyperscale and colo — often excluded or sub-limited on damage-triggered BI towers.
Anonymised: Gate 2 campus on flexible connection — energy underwriter priced damage BI; tenant SLA penalties from curtailment sat uninsured on London tower.
Open economics with: what is most mispriced on a GB energy account today — then admit scope limits before answering with register-backed evidence.

Ofgem demand-reform evidence (Feb 2026) cites NESO CFI finding ~140 data-centre projects (~50 GW) in the transmission demand queue, with ~71 (~20 GW) reporting financial commitment and FID — mature load seeking firm dates while accepting flexible terms.

NESO Demand CFI (Mar 2026 summary) received 243 responses representing ~93 GW demand capability; data centres account for 55% of project phases and ~51 GW of stated MW — dominant technology in the reform evidence base.
Contracted demand-queue offers surged from 41 GW (Nov 2024) to 125 GW (Jun 2025) while GB peak demand on 11 Feb 2026 was 45 GW — queue scale exceeds contemporaneous system peak by nearly 3×.

From 21 Nov 2025 the TEC register includes a Gate column (Gate 1 / Gate 2) populated only after countersigned reform agreements — objective firmness signal for transmission-connected assets pending full queue reform.

Ofgem Connect pillar (Feb 2026) is considering flexible, non-firm, or ramped connection conditions specifically for data centres as demand scale threatens operability — regulatory path from voluntary flex to mandated curtailment terms.

NESO FY2024/25 balancing spend totalled £2.7bn (+10% y/y); thermal constraint costs rose 64% to £1.7bn on 13.5 TWh constraint volumes (+81% y/y) — Scotland outages and congestion amplified bid actions on wind.

Wind curtailment reached 13% of hypothetical wind outturn in FY2024/25 (up from 8% prior year) as Scottish thermal limits and planned reinforcement outages coincided with high wind — frequency proxy for non-firm interruption severity.

NESO 2025 Annual Balancing Costs Report projects balancing costs peaking ~£8bn by 2030 under current trends, with up to ~£4bn avoidable if critical network projects deliver on CP30 timelines — constraint costs dominate the upward path.

2025 non-firm connection review identifies four predominant models — capacity-limited, time-limited, dynamic operating envelopes, and fully flexible ANM access — with pilots citing up to ~80% connection-cost reduction and ~50% lead-time reduction versus firm reinforcement paths.

Non-firm curtailment allocation rules span LIFO (newer connections curtailed first), pro-rata (shared proportional cut), and curtailment-index thresholds — predictability of rule choice directly maps to trigger_gap and basis-risk design for availability cover.

Curtailment Credit Market simulations (2026 preprint) show total value of served load 1.41–1.83× higher than pro-rata administrative curtailment when VOLL spans ~$4k–$667k/MWh across heterogeneous loads including data centres on non-firm interconnection.

Orkney OPF case study (2010) quantifies non-firm curtailment frequency and duration via time-series analysis: new onshore wind faced ~49% annual production loss under network constraints; tidal ~24%; wave ~5% — template for E[L] pricing from register-backed firmness flags.

Industry survey frames NDBI as a widening coverage gap: supply-chain stress, pandemic disruption, and weather variability produce revenue or cost shocks without property damage, yet standard indemnity BI often attaches only after physical loss.

Direct-to-chip liquid cooling is shifting the loss mix: liquid-related events account for nearly one-quarter of historical data-centre loss costs, including sprinkler leakage and escaped coolant — a physical-damage channel distinct from grid NDBI but relevant to integrated power/cooling underwriting.

Swiss Re engineering modelling puts a single hyperscale site nat-cat tail in the order of ~$10bn insured loss — financing pressure for full TIV limits runs into re/insurer capacity that can only support a fraction at competitive traditional rates.

Broker guidance treats long-term PPAs, behind-the-meter generation, and baseload partnerships as dependency traps: they shift the enterprise failure curve toward regulatory shutdown, fuel disruption, or off-site utility behaviour with no on-site damage.

London Market BI model wordings embed a material-damage proviso: interruption indemnity typically requires loss, destruction, or damage to scheduled property and an admitted claim under the companion property policy before BI adjusts.

Rating-agency research on hyperscale campuses ($20–50bn construction-phase TIV) finds programmes increasingly capped at PML or MFL layers — insured limits often reach only one-third to one-half of total campus value, with remainder retained or captived.

SLA parametric for colocation specifies pre-agreed payout amounts on telemetry-verified breach of lease uptime metrics, with guaranteed settlement within ~40 days — designed to bypass forensic BI adjustment and SLA credit disputes.

Descartes parametric DC suite offers up to $140m per policy across ~20 nat-cat perils, explicitly covering NDBI, DSU, SLA penalties, and behind-the-meter generation — positioned as deductible/top-up liquidity rather than full indemnity replacement.

UK broker SLA parametric framing ties fixed payouts to lease-defined uptime, power continuity, and connectivity thresholds — including tenant termination following repeated breach — and can aggregate across a portfolio for London accumulation control.

Clarke (2016): under DARA, rational index-hedge size is capped below full insurance because downside basis risk r (loss without payout) and premium load must be weighed against marginal risk reduction — unlike indemnity where infinite risk aversion implies full cover.

Teh–Woolnough (2019): higher loss–index correlation is an insufficient quality metric; partial-order ranking must separate upside basis risk q (payout without loss) from downside r (loss without payout) when selecting triggers for heterogeneous buyers.

Maier–Scherer expectile framework: for a fixed register or telemetry index, basis-risk-minimizing parametric payouts are conditional expectiles of true loss given trigger — implementable via asymmetric least-squares regression on step or linear payout functions.

Anonymised placement: a transmission-connected AI campus at Gate 2 on a flexible import arrangement — property and DSU priced on damage triggers; when the operator issued a lawful curtailment instruction with zero asset damage, the London energy tower paid nothing while tenant SLA credits ran for the full curtailed window.

Anonymised placement: a wholesale broker bound a colo operator's damage-BI and cyber tower on tier certification and MFL; SLA service credits for a sub-hour voltage sag sat outside every trigger until a separate parametric SLA layer was manuscripted to mirror lease uptime metrics.

Anonymised placement: a flexible-connected onshore wind asset in Scotland — generation fully operational but pro-rata curtailed at a constraint boundary; revenue shortfall was treated as a merchant/market exposure while the adjacent data-centre programme in the same T-zone was still quoted standard property BI without an availability index.

Anonymised placement pattern on London energy accounts: submissions still lead with square footage and tier class while underwriters quietly ask for PPA, behind-the-meter, and grid-dependency maps — the gap between energy-strategy manuscript and damage-triggered BI is where curtailment NDBI is either excluded or sub-limited.

Broker research frames grid curtailment, regulatory shutdown of an offtaker, and fuel-supply disruption as the core data-centre exposure today — business interruption without physical damage — and documents sophisticated buyers negotiating utility-failure NDBI, Tier-1 CBI on energy providers, and parametric grid-outage duration triggers.

Marsh UK Cyber SLA parametric for data centres ties triggers to lease-agreement metrics — uptime percentage, power continuity, cooling, connectivity — with fixed payouts over predefined periods rather than forensic BI adjustment; cover can be per-facility or aggregated across a portfolio for London Market accumulation control.

Cyber accumulation stress tests diverge by orders of magnitude across governments, model vendors, and market-wide scenarios — one European reinsurer's underwriting leadership argued correlated cyber portfolios remain too opaque to price confidently, yet capacity continues to deploy — the disagreement itself signals architectural not data gap.

snippets.claim: Argument move: an AI-insurance MGA path prices by importing incumbent claims history and checkbox workflow controls rather than modelling novel peril from scratch — capital efficiency comes from reinsurer backing plus scale across uncorrelated lines, not from holding balance sheet.

Argument move: interruption without damage is not an edge case — dozens of >$1bn NDBI events catalogued from nat cat and infrastructure failure — parametric products that reached meaningful London Market adoption typically needed 3–5 years from launch, a generational cycle not a quarterly product tweak.

style_notes.nfri_application: Table PML/basis-risk estimates for curtailment at a constraint boundary — cite Lloyd's RDS, academic CCM papers, and broker grid studies where figures diverge.
If damage-BI underprices availability loss, whitespace carriers and parametric MGAs earn; if market overprices via blanket exclusions, sidelined names look cheap for wrong reason.
Layer Swiss Re premium runway ($10.6→$24bn), S&P PML/MFL partial-TIV bands, and single-site nat-cat tail (~$10bn) in one table — show financing demand diverging from attachable capacity.
Map BI 1.0 (material-damage proviso) → 2.0 (SLA/parametric telemetry) → 3.0 (register-index curtailment) using Parametrix, Marsh UK, and Descartes product shapes as contemporaneous 2.0 anchors.
Score candidate curtailment indices on Teh–Woolnough upside q and downside r separately — a high-correlation NESO constraint signal can still fail on downside r for a specific account P&L.

Paraphrase reinsurer cyber-accumulation opacity quotes into a table of curtailment-severity estimates at shared constraint boundaries — cite Lloyd's RDS market stress alongside register-backed frequencies.

Field notes open analysis with four anonymised placement vignettes — Gate 2 campus, colo SLA gap, flexible wind curtailment, London energy account split — each followed within one sentence by LMA BI trigger or register fact.

argument_moves: Interruption without damage is not edge case — it is the core nat-cat and infrastructure NDBI story (Instech parametric post).
Firmness is migrating from qualitative broker narrative to register fact (TEC/ECR + Apr 2023 SCR) — repricing moment.
Cyber cat debate shows markets can disagree 100× on accumulation — grid curtailment lacks even that debate because no event set exists.
Demand queue MW now dwarfs system peak (125 GW queue vs ~45 GW peak Feb 2026) — repricing must treat firmness as scarce capacity, not binary grid access.
81% CFI appetite for phased/non-firm plus Connect-pillar conditions for data centres signal a generational shift from optional flex to contractually mandated curtailment exposure on large loads.

FY2024/25 constraint economics (£1.7bn thermal, 13% wind curtailment) provide an observable macro proxy; academic pro-rata vs market allocation (1.4–1.8× welfare gap) explains why blunt rules destroy insurable surplus at the constraint boundary.
TEC Gate column (Nov 2025) and Apr 2023 DNO curtailment-limit standardisation convert firmness from broker narrative to register-visible contract fields — the measurement substrate NFRI scores.

Orkney OPF losses (49%/24%) prove curtailment severity is locational and technology-specific; snapshot firm-connection studies systematically over-state headroom — honest scope limit for index triggers.
Energy strategy is now underwriting input: PPAs, behind-the-meter plant, and grid curtailment move failure modes off the damage-BI trigger entirely (EPIC energy-risk curve).
Hyperscale finance asks for TIV; London Market answers with PML/MFL layers — the uninsured middle is structural whitespace for parametric NDBI and SLA mirrors (S&P + Swiss Re).
Basis-risk literature does not forbid parametric cover — it bounds rational hedge size and demands trigger design beyond correlation (Clarke r, Teh–Woolnough q/r, expectile payout calibration).
Parametric DC products explicitly stack as deductible fill, DSU liquidity, and SLA penalty cover — not as forensic BI replacement (Descartes + Parametrix + Marsh UK framing).
Interruption without damage is the mainstream NDBI story — parametric is how the market closes triggers conventional BI cannot reach (Instech parametric post).
MGA economics: price and distribute without balance sheet; import human-line claims history to underwrite novel exposure — checkbox controls gate capacity (Strata AI-insurance investigation).
Cyber accumulation PML debate spans 100× across institutions — grid curtailment lacks even that debate because no correlatable event set exists at the constraint boundary.
London energy accounts split: damage-BI towers on tier and MFL while energy-dependency and SLA credits require manuscript parametric layers (EPIC energy risk curve; Marsh UK SLA parametric).
